thread:
Maria Chen: hey team, customer reported embeddings API error when sending a batch of 4 vectors. error: "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768". they're using model "text-embedding-ada-002" (we think) but the client library was generating 768-dim vectors. can someone advise quick root cause + mitigation? this is blocking a production job.

Sam Ortiz: can you paste the exact request body (sanitized) and the model name + model version? also need the request_id from the response headers if available. :eyes:

Maria Chen: here's the sanitized payload and error from logs (request_id: rq_02b8f4c3):
```json
{
  "model": "text-embedding-ada-002",
  "input": ["I love redwood!", "how to scale embeddings"],
  "vectors": [[...768 floats...],[...768 floats...],[...768 floats...],[...768 floats...]],
  "batch_size": 4
}
```
error: "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768"

Devon Li: most likely cause: client is producing 768-dim vectors (maybe using a different embedding model locally) but the server-side model expects 1536. common mismatch: newer ada variants have 1536, older ones 768. quick checks: 
- verify model catalog: `GET /v1/models/text-embedding-ada-002` -> check `embedding_dim`
- verify client library config (maybe defaulting to `small-embedding` variant)

Priya Singh: for support runbook/triage: steps to repro + file a ticket if customer is P1/P2. minimal repro we ask for: curl request + raw error + request_id + approximate timestamp + region. also ask whether they use any gateway/proxy that might be modifying payloads (some proxies collapse arrays). I'll start the handoff doc here. :ticket:

embed-runbook-bot: Runbook: /runbooks/embeddings/dimension-mismatch — includes common causes (wrong model, padded vs concatenated vectors, JSON encoding truncation), quick mitigation (validate vector length pre-send, reject at gateway), and sample curl with shape assertions.

Maria Chen: adding the curl we used to repro (sanitized). note: client SDK had automatic retry enabled; customer said they saw duplicate billing events when the client retried after a client-side timeout.
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-ada-002","input":["a","b","c","d"],"vectors":[[...768...],[...768...],[...768...],[...768...]]}'
```
response: 400 {"error":"dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768","request_id":"rq_02b8f4c3"}

Sam Ortiz: immediate mitigation options:
- tell customer to send only `input` and let our embeddings endpoint compute vectors (avoid sending precomputed vectors) OR
- if they must send precomputed vectors, add a validation layer (API Gateway or edge lambda) to assert `vector.length == model_dim` before forwarding.
- disable automatic retries for embeddings until we confirm idempotency/dup protection.

Sam Ortiz: I'm escalating to eng-runtime (assigning to @Devon). setting severity P2 because production job is impacted but there is a clear repro and workaround. creating internal ticket: RI-ENT-5342. attaching logs + repro curl + request_id.

Devon Li: got it, looking now. quick followups:
- Maria, can you confirm whether the customer passed `vectors` in the request body intentionally? most customers just pass `input`.
- also, which SDK and version did they use? older SDKs had a bug that serialized floats with lower precision causing truncation for some encodings.

Maria Chen: they intentionally precomputed vectors (third-party pipeline) and are batching to avoid extra compute. SDK: node-embedder v0.9.1. they have a proxy that might be re-serializing JSON (we're checking).

Devon Li: next steps I will own:
1) add validation on the ingress path in Dedicated/Hosted to reject `vectors` whose length != model_dim with a clearer error message (include expected_dim in response). quick fix rollout to edge 2hrs (can be hotfix).
2) update docs/FAQ: example section about "precomputed vectors must match model dim" + sample code to assert length before sending (I'll add snippet).
3) recommend runtime configuration: enable continuous batching with `max_batch_latency_ms=25` and `max_batch_size=256` for higher throughput without client-side precompute. add note about tradeoff latency vs cost.
4) ticket RI-ENT-5342 opened with proposed patch and rollout plan.

Priya Singh: for the customer-facing support reply, recommended message: short explanation + workaround + ask for logs + advise to disable retries. e.g.,
"Thanks — the error means your precomputed vectors are the wrong size for the model you selected. Please either (1) send raw text to the embeddings endpoint and let it compute vectors, or (2) ensure each vector length equals the model embedding dim (1536 for text-embedding-ada-002). Also please disable automatic retries while we investigate to avoid duplicate billing. We've opened ticket RI-ENT-5342."

Maria Chen: sending that now. will post customer ack when I get it. thanks everyone. :rocket:

Devon Li: follow-up doc snippet I'll add to support FAQ: code to validate in Node prior to send:
```js
function validateVectors(vecs, expectedDim){
  for(const v of vecs){
    if(v.length !== expectedDim) throw new Error(`vector dim ${v.length} != expected ${expectedDim}`)
  }
}
// call validateVectors(payload.vectors, 1536)
```
Also note: for high throughput, prefer server-side batching -> less client compute + consistent billing. I'll push the doc update in the next hour.
